title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

Peak Adoption Rate Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting maximum mask adoption during intervention

Time-to-Peak Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting the time lag from intervention to peak behavior change

key_patterns.name: Multiplex network with three layers
key_patterns.description: Agents connect via family, work/school, and community layers; an aggregate 'all' list is present per agent.
key_patterns.relevance: Layered influence enables differential contagion of behavior; weights per layer should be calibrated to reflect stronger intra-family effects.

key_patterns.name: Heterogeneous risk perception
key_patterns.description: Each agent has a risk_perception in [0,1], likely continuous and skewed; higher values associate with greater baseline mask adoption.
key_patterns.relevance: Risk perception should modulate individual susceptibility to adopt/persist in mask-wearing.

key_patterns.name: Seeded adoption at t=0
key_patterns.description: initial_mask_wearing and day 0 wearing_mask indicate a non-zero initial adopter set.
key_patterns.relevance: Initial conditions drive early diffusion; seed prevalence should be matched in simulation initialization.

key_patterns.name: Information exposure influences adoption
key_patterns.description: received_info on a day increases the probability of adoption on that or subsequent days.
key_patterns.relevance: A distinct exogenous information pathway needs to be modeled in addition to peer effects.

key_patterns.name: Behavioral persistence
key_patterns.description: Agents wearing masks at t-1 have elevated probability to continue wearing at t relative to non-wearers adopting.
key_patterns.relevance: Include state dependence (habit inertia) to reproduce persistence and reversion rates.

key_patterns.name: Degree heterogeneity across layers
key_patterns.description: family_connections, work_school_connections, and community_connections vary by agent; total_connections = sum of layers.
key_patterns.relevance: Heterogeneous degree drives exposure heterogeneity; simulation must preserve per-layer degree sequences.

key_patterns.name: Demographic modulation of contacts
key_patterns.description: occupation and age_group likely correlate with layer-specific degrees (e.g., students in work/school layer, retirees in community/family).
key_patterns.relevance: Contact schedules and influence weights may be conditioned on occupation/age to better match real mixing patterns.

key_patterns.name: Edge directionality and reciprocity
key_patterns.description: Adjacency lists are not guaranteed reciprocal; edges can be treated as directed or symmetrized.
key_patterns.relevance: Choice affects clustering and diffusion speed; symmetrization typically increases mutual reinforcement.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception distribution
key_distributions.description: Continuous on [0,1], suitable for Beta distribution.
key_distributions.parameters: Beta(a,b); estimate via method-of-moments from agent_attributes.risk_perception

key_distributions.name: Layer-specific degree distributions
key_distributions.description: Non-negative integers per layer; often overdispersed vs Poisson; Negative Binomial is a good fit if var>mean.
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L in {family, work_school, community}: mean_L, var_L, optionally NB(k_L, p_L) fitted from agent_attributes or from social_network adjacency lengths

key_distributions.name: Adoption and persistence probabilities
key_distributions.description: Transition probabilities conditional on prior state and info.
key_distributions.parameters: P10_info = P(mask_t=1|mask_{t-1}=0, info_t=1); P10_noinfo = P(mask_t=1|mask_{t-1}=0, info_t=0); P11_info = P(mask_t=1|mask_{t-1}=1, info_t=1); P11_noinfo = P(mask_t=1|mask_{t-1}=1, info_t=0); derive from train_data

key_relationships.relationship: Positive association; higher risk_perception increases probability of initial adoption.
key_relationships.strength: Expected moderate to strong; quantify via logistic regression at day 0.

key_relationships.relationship: Information exposure increases adoption probability among non-wearers.
State dependence; prior wearing predicts current wearing.
Occupational and age categories correlate with layer degrees (e.g., students with higher work/school degree).
key_relationships.strength: Moderate; assess via ANOVA or regression on degree counts.

key_relationships.relationship: Family interactions carry stronger influence than work/school, which is stronger than community.
key_relationships.strength: Assumption to be calibrated; start with family > work/school > community.

risk_perception_distribution.notes: Compute a,b via method-of-moments; use to sample missing values or to parameterize susceptibility scaling.

initial_mask_prevalence.notes: Use exact agent-level initial states when available; p0 for consistency checks and synthetic agents.

susceptibility_scaling_by_risk.notes: Multiplier on social influence/logit; higher values increase sensitivity to risk.

layer_weights.notes: Relative influence weights; refine via SMM/ABC to match observed adoption dynamics.

edge_directionality.notes: Symmetrize adjacency for undirected influence; improves realism of mutual influence and clustering.

degree_sequence_by_layer.value: Use agent_attributes layer counts or lengths of social_network adjacency lists per layer to set configuration model targets
degree_sequence_by_layer.notes: Prefer explicit edges from social_network; validate against totals in agent_attributes.

contact_rate_per_layer_per_day.source: Assumption; tune to match adoption speed
contact_rate_per_layer_per_day.notes: Expected daily effective influence contacts; can be modeled as Poisson(λ_L).

update_rule.value: Logistic adoption with inertia: P(mask_t=1) = sigmoid(α0 + α_persist*mask_{t-1} + α_info*info_t + α_risk*(risk_perception - mean_risk) + Σ_L w_L * frac_masked_neighbors_L)
update_rule.source: Model design informed by train_data.csv and network layers
update_rule.notes: Set α and w via calibration; frac_masked_neighbors_L computed from neighbors’ states.

alpha0_intercept.value: Estimate via logistic regression on train_data with info_t and mask_{t-1}
alpha0_intercept.notes: Represents baseline propensity absent info and peers.

alpha_persist.notes: Captures habit persistence controlling for info.

alpha_info.notes: Direct effect of information on adoption among prior non-wearers.

social_influence_strength.source: Fitted to match aggregate prevalence trajectory using network
social_influence_strength.notes: Scales the contribution of Σ_L w_L * frac_masked_neighbors_L in the logit.

reversion_noise.notes: Captures random lapses independent of peers and info.

daily_info_probability.notes: Use as exogenous broadcast rate if no endogenous mechanism; or as target rate when combining endogenous/exogenous sources.

endogenous_info_from_neighbors.notes: Allows info to diffuse via network; tune θ so simulated mean info rate matches r_info.

info_effect_lag.value: k_lag ∈ {0,1,2} days; select via AIC/BIC from lagged logistic models
info_effect_lag.notes: Incorporate if lagged info improves predictive power.

initial_states.value: Use day 0 wearing_mask per agent if available; else agent_attributes.initial_mask_wearing

mapping_ids.value: Ensure consistent integer IDs across files; convert JSON string keys to int
mapping_ids.notes: Alignment is critical for agent attributes and network edges.

occupation_modifiers.notes: Optional adjustments; calibrate or disable if not improving fit.

preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure booleans and integers are correctly read; convert JSON string IDs to integers.
Check that 'all' equals union(family, work_school, community) and deduplicate neighbor lists.

preprocessing_steps.step: Decide on edge directionality and symmetrize if needed
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Make graph representation consistent with chosen influence model.

preprocessing_steps.step: Compute per-layer degrees and distribution fits
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Estimate mean/variance and fit Poisson/NB to inform contact processes.
Estimate P10_info, P10_noinfo, P11_info, P11_noinfo, and reversion rates.
Fit logistic models of wearing_mask_t on mask_{t-1}, received_info_t, risk_perception (and lags) to get α coefficients.
Compute daily mask prevalence to serve as calibration and validation target.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Two-stage approach: (1) Micro-transition calibration using train_data. Fit logistic regression for wearing_mask_t with predictors mask_{t-1}, received_info_t, risk_perception (and optional lags), yielding α0, α_persist, α_info, α_risk. (2) Network influence calibration using simulated method of moments or ABC. Run the agent-based simulation on the actual multilayer graph, varying social influence strength γ, layer weights w_L, and contact rates λ_L to match observed moments: daily prevalence curve, adoption and reversion rates, and info exposure rate. Optionally include occupation/age modifiers and select via information criteria or cross-validation.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Hold out a temporal segment (e.g., last 20% days) or a random subset of agents. Validate on: (a) Aggregate prevalence trajectory (RMSE/MAE), (b) Transition probabilities in holdout (calibration curve, Brier score), (c) Persistence and reversion rates, (d) Sensitivity analyses across edge directionality and layer weights. Perform posterior predictive checks if using ABC/Bayesian methods.

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Structure and type
  - Flat CSV; one row per agent (no nested structures).
  - Primary key: agent_id (integer, unique).
  - Static attributes; no timestamps or explicit edges.

- Column meanings
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for each agent.
  - age: Integer age.
  - age_group: Categorical age bracket (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age).
  - occupation: Categorical role (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar) informing work/school layer participation.
  - risk_perception: Float in [0,1] representing personal perceived risk; higher implies greater propensity to adopt mask-wearing.
  - initial_mask_wearing: Boolean seed state for mask adoption at t=0.
  - family_connections: Integer count of ties in family layer.
  - work_school_connections: Integer count of ties in work/school layer.
  - community_connections: Integer count of ties in community/social layer (neighbors, acquaintances, public interactions).
  - total_connections: Integer, equals family + work_school + community; serves as a consistency check and overall degree.

- Relationships and layers
  - No explicit network edges; only per-layer degree counts. Implies a multiplex network with three layers: family, work/school, community.
  - total_connections is a derived field from the three layer-specific degrees; no additional nesting or grouping (e.g., households) is present.

- How to use in the simulation
  - Agent initialization: Create one Agent object per row with attributes: demographics (age, age_group, occupation), psychological (risk_perception), and behavioral state (mask_wearing initialized from initial_mask_wearing).
  - Network construction: For each layer, generate edges to match the degree sequence (e.g., configuration model) and optionally weight layers differently (family > work/school > community) for influence/contact frequency. total_connections can validate sums.
  - Behavior dynamics: At each step, update mask_wearing based on:
    - Social influence: proportion of masked neighbors per layer (with layer-specific weights).
    - Individual trait: risk_perception as a baseline propensity or as a coefficient in an adoption function (e.g., logistic/threshold).
    - Demographic/occupation modifiers: occupation and age_group can modulate exposure/influence strength in work/school vs. other layers.
  - Seeding and calibration: initial_mask_wearing defines initial adopters; risk_perception distribution and degree counts shape early adoption and diffusion speed.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json

- Data structure and type:
  - JSON object representing a multilayer social network as adjacency lists.
  - Top-level: mapping from agent IDs (stringified integers, range appears to be 0–999) to an object of contact lists.

- Meaning of keys:
  - Each top-level key: a unique agent/person ID.
  - Nested keys within each agent:
    - family: list of agent IDs representing familial contacts.
    - work_school: list of agent IDs representing workplace or school contacts.
    - community: list of agent IDs representing broader community/social contacts.
    - all: union of the above lists (appears deduplicated), i.e., all known contacts for that agent.

- Relationships and nested elements:
  - Each nested list is an adjacency list for that layer; entries are integer IDs referencing other agents.
  - Edges are given from the perspective of the focal agent; reciprocity is not guaranteed by the data (treat as directed unless symmetrized).
  - No weights, timestamps, or frequencies are included; no self-loops observed in the sample.
  - The “all” list is a derived convenience field; it should equal the deduplicated union of family ∪ work_school ∪ community.

- How this informs simulation entities and interactions:
  - Agents: instantiate one agent per top-level key; store mask-wearing state and any behavioral parameters externally (not in this file).
  - Network layers: construct three layers (family, work_school, community) to enable layer-specific influence/interaction rules; optionally also an aggregate network from “all.”
  - Interaction modeling:
    - Use layer membership to set contact probabilities, frequencies, or influence strengths (e.g., family > work/school > community).
    - Decide on edge directionality: either use as directed (as-is) or symmetrize for undirected interactions.
    - Sample daily interactions per agent from the relevant layer lists according to your schedule/policy.
  - Initialization/validation:
    - Convert string keys to integers for consistency.
    - Verify that “all” equals the union of the three layers; recompute if needed.
    - Check and deduplicate neighbor lists if required by your engine.
  - Scale: IDs suggest a population of approximately 1,000 agents, suitable for agent-based simulation over multilayer contacts.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv

- Overall structure and type:
  - CSV file in long-format panel (time-series per agent).
  - Each row is an agent-day observation; multiple rows per agent across days.
  - Composite primary key: (agent_id, day).

- Columns and meanings:
  - day (int): Discrete simulation time index (t = 0,1,2,...).
  - agent_id (int): Unique identifier for an agent.
  - wearing_mask (bool): Agent’s behavioral state on that day (true = wearing a mask).
  - received_info (bool): Whether the agent received pro-mask information on that day (source unspecified).

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - No nested structures; flat table.
  - Temporal dependency is implicit: state at day t can depend on states/events at t-1.
  - No social network topology or neighbor relationships included; info source and contagion pathways are not encoded.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Agent state variables:
    - wearing_mask_t: behavioral state to initialize or validate against.
    - info_flag_t: exogenous/endogenous information event indicator; can seed “information memory.”
  - Transition modeling:
    - Calibrate per-day transition probabilities P(mask_t | mask_{t-1}, info_t) from the panel:
      - Adoption: P(mask_t = 1 | mask_{t-1} = 0, info_t).
      - Persistence: P(mask_t = 1 | mask_{t-1} = 1, info_t).
      - Reversion: P(mask_t = 0 | mask_{t-1} = 1, info_t = 0).
      - Spontaneous adoption: P(mask_t = 1 | mask_{t-1} = 0, info_t = 0).
    - Optionally estimate lags: P(mask_t | info_{t-k}) to capture delayed effects.
    - Allow heterogeneity by agent_id if data permit (random effects or per-agent propensities).
  - Simulation initialization:
    - Use day 0 rows to set initial mask-wearing states; optionally bootstrap info flags if present.
  - Network dynamics integration:
    - Since network edges are absent, introduce or import a social graph; model received_info_t as:
      - Exogenous broadcast process calibrated from observed info rates, and/or
      - Endogenous diffusion from neighbors (e.g., threshold or weighted influence); fit parameters so that simulated P(mask_t) trajectories match the panel.
  - Validation targets:
    - Match aggregate prevalence over time, switching rates, and persistence measured from this file.
  - Data handling notes:
    - Booleans stored as true/false; ensure correct parsing.
    - Check for missing days per agent; if gaps exist, treat as skipped time steps or impute.
